claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its subsets are governed by local lattice distortion induced by atomic size mismatch.
Local lattice distortion affects dislocation motion.
Changes in dislocation motion caused by local lattice distortion determine strength and ductility.
The investigated Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloy and its selected quaternary and ternary subsets can be processed into single-phase FCC structures.
Systematically changing the constituent elements produces different levels of atomic size mismatch.
Thermomechanical processing can maintain a single-phase FCC structure across the proposed alloy series.
A consistent processing history will provide sufficiently comparable microstructures for mechanical-property comparisons.
Atomic size mismatch calculated from atomic radii is an adequate measure of local lattice distortion.
Increasing atomic size mismatch increases local lattice distortion.
Greater local lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion.
Greater atomic size mismatch may reduce ductility by producing localized stress concentrations.
Alloys with higher atomic size mismatch will have greater yield strength than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Alloys with higher atomic size mismatch will have lower ductility than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
The proposed mechanism applies only to single-phase FCC alloys derived from the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system and within the atomic-size-mismatch range compatible with FCC stability.
Electronic structure and short-range ordering may also contribute to mechanical-property differences.
